claim: Mulligan a seven with two lands unless it also has a mana rock and at least two plays castable off those three sources. Even with the rock, play the rock on turn 2 and expect to sit on three sources for several turns: this list has 36 lands and its payoffs cost 4 to 6.
evidence: Game 0034: it kept Mountain + Marsh Flats + Talisman of Conviction and missed land drops on rounds 3, 5 and 6, never getting past 3 lands. Only Sol Ring and a foretold Sozin's Comet rescued it. Game 0032's two-lander worked only because Legion Leadership was a third land.

Game 0012 kept 2 lands plus Signet and Talisman of Conviction: no missed land drops, Zuko in round 4, win. Game 0023 kept 2 lands plus Talisman of Conviction: no missed drops, but Zuko waited until round 4 because Talisman of Hierarchy was the only W/B source in round 3.

claim: Hold X spells and pump for combat, and plan every turn you attack with Zuko around a way to spend the firebending red, because it empties at end of combat. Good ways: flash in Embercleave (it costs {1} less per attacker), Electrodominance with a big X (which also casts a free spell from hand), Invoke Calamity, The Last Agni Kai.
evidence: Game 0032 round 4: firebending red paid for Embercleave, making Zuko a 6/8 double striker for 12. Game 0034 round 6: a 26-red pool cast Electrodominance X=22, which knocked Choco out of the game, and its free cast put Ozai onto the battlefield. Game 0033 round 5: 6 firebending red emptied unused because the hand had nothing to spend it on.

Game 0021, round 5: Electro held Zuko's RR, and after combat Tavern Brawler was cast from Laelia's exile, putting a counter on each creature. Game 0012, round 7: Tyrant held 4 red. Two paid for Avatar's Wrath from exile, one paid Esika's Rhystic tax, and the last helped recast Zuko from exile for {2}.

Game 0042, round 4: Zuko's {R}{R} paid for Great Train Heist's base cost plus the Treasure mode, aimed at Miirym. Scarlett connected, and the Treasure paid for Avatar Roku the next turn. Game 0041, rounds 5 to 7: with nothing to cast, the pilot put every leftover firebending red into Turret charge counters.

Game 0052, round 8 (table turn 29): Zuko's firebending 5 and the 4 red Fire Nation Palace gave Heartfire Hero made 9 red. {R}{R} paid for Blazing Crescendo on Zuko, who had Embercleave, and he hit for 8 double strike (16 commander damage) to knock out The Wise Mothman. The other 7 red paid for Commune with Lava at X=5. Game 0051, round 4: Zuko's 2 red paid for Haste Magic, and he hit for 5.

claim: Your biggest turn is foretelling Sozin's Comet with spare mana, then casting it from exile for {2}{R} with Isshin on the battlefield. The cast from exile puts a counter on each creature through Zuko, and Isshin makes every firebending trigger happen twice. Keep an X spell in hand for that attack.
evidence: Game 0034: on round 5 it foretold the Comet off Sol Ring. On round 6 it cast the Comet from exile and attacked with Zuko, Daydreamer and Isshin. The doubled firebending triggers gave it 26 red, enough for Electrodominance X=22 on Choco at 22 life.

claim: Norin the Wary is a Zuko engine. Every time any player casts a spell or a creature attacks, Norin is exiled, and it returns at the next end step. That counts as a permanent entering from exile, so if Zuko is on the battlefield, every creature you control gets a +1/+1 counter. Cast Norin before Zuko, and resolve the Zuko trigger on every return.
evidence: Game 0032 round 3: Zuko was cast, Norin was exiled by that cast and returned at the end step, and Zuko became 3/5 immediately. By round 4 Zuko had 3 counters without any other exile card.

claim: While Zuko is on the battlefield, always take Goliath Daydreamer's free recast from exile, even when it does nothing (Electrodominance with X=0). Casting a spell from exile puts a +1/+1 counter on each of your creatures. Daydreamer only re-exiles spells cast from hand, so the recast copy goes to the graveyard.
evidence: Game 0033: on round 3 the pilot declined the X=0 recast because Zuko was not out. On round 4, with Zuko out, the same X=0 Electrodominance gave every creature a counter, and on round 5 the Hex Magic recast did too. Game 0034 round 6: the X=0 Electrodominance recast added another counter.

claim: Ozai has indestructible while you hold six or more unspent mana, and he turns mana you would lose into red. When removal targets him, tap lands in response to reach six floating, and do not dump the pool below six on your own turn.
evidence: Game 0033 round 7: Hearthhull cast Putrefy on Ozai while the pool held 5. The pilot tapped a Mountain in response to reach 6, and Ozai survived. The auditor confirmed the pool should be kept (14 R) from turn to turn.

claim: Cast haste creatures in main phase 1, before you move to combat. Laelia, the Blade Reforged, Iroh, Headliner Scarlett and Hellkite Charger all lose their first attack, and Laelia loses her exile trigger, if they come down after combat.
evidence: Game 0021, round 4 (table turn 13): the pilot cast Talisman, attacked with Zuko alone for 2, then cast Laelia in main 2. It wrote that it 'meant to cast Laelia before combat so she could attack'. In game 0012, round 3, the pilot cast Laelia before combat; her attack exiled Arid Mesa, which became that turn's land drop.

Game 0042, round 4: Scarlett was cast in main 1 and aimed at Miirym. The Dragon token could not block, so Zuko killed Sarkhan Unbroken and Scarlett hit for 3. Game 0041, round 7: Hellkite Charger was cast in main 1 and attacked that turn for 7 in the air.

claim: Party Thrasher is an engine for Zuko. Each first main phase, discard a dead card to exile the top two, and take a land or cheap spell. Cast Zuko before you play the chosen card, because a land played from exile puts a counter on every creature. Noncreature spells you cast from exile have convoke, so tap Thrasher, Avatar Roku and other red creatures to pay for them.
evidence: Game 0023, round 4: the pilot cast Zuko, then played Bloodstained Mire from Thrasher's exile, and Zuko triggered. In round 6 Thrasher exiled Delayed Blast Fireball. It was cast from exile, paid by one Mountain plus convoking Roku and Thrasher, and dealt 5 to each opponent and their creatures, killing all but one opposing creature. Aggravated Assault was then convoked from exile with Zuko.

claim: Storm King's Thunder followed by Chandra's Ignition on your biggest creature hits every opponent (X+1) times for that creature's power. Pay for Thunder with the firebending red after combat damage, then cast Ignition from lands in main 2, and cast no other instant or sorcery between the two. Ignition also hits your own other creatures, Zuko included, so only fire it when it is lethal.
evidence: Game 0012, round 8 (table turn 30): Storm King's Thunder with X=3 was paid with RRR floating plus Plains, Swamp and Talisman. Chandra's Ignition on a 5-power Laelia then hit four times, 20 to each opponent, killing Tidus (12) and Esika (19). Zuko and Leyline Tyrant died to the copies.

claim: When Zuko attacks with Avatar Roku on the battlefield, put Zuko's firebending trigger on the stack first so Roku's six red resolves first. Spend that red on Roku's {R}{R}{R}: +3/+0 aimed at Zuko while the firebending trigger is still on the stack. X is Zuko's power when the trigger resolves, so every pump also makes more red. Six red makes Zuko 8 power and firebending then adds 8 red. That buys two more Roku pumps plus Legion Leadership: 28 commander damage from a single attack.
evidence: Game 0042, round 5 (table turn 20): Roku's trigger resolved first, but the pilot let Zuko's firebending resolve at power 2 before pumping. So it made only {R}{R}. The total of 8 red paid for two Roku pumps and Legion Leadership, and Zuko hit Wilhelt for 16. With the pumps before firebending, Zuko could have dealt 28, and 21 commander damage kills. The pilot wrote in its notes: 'pump Zuko with Roku mana BEFORE firebending trigger resolves'. Wilhelt survived and killed this seat three turns later.

claim: Before keeping, check that the hand can make {R}{W}{B} by turn 3 or 4. White is the colour this list runs short of, and Zuko, Isshin and Swords to Plowshares all need it. A seven whose lands are only Mountains, Swamps and red lands has only its mono-red spells to cast. If that is one or two spells, mulligan, because the first mulligan is free.
evidence: Game 0041: it kept Knoll, Mountain, Mountain, Swamp, Isshin, Swords and March of Reckless Joy. It never found white in 7 rounds and ended the game with Zuko uncast and Isshin and Swords still in hand, while The Wise Mothman milled away Roku, Ozai, Etali and Sozin's Comet. Game 0042: it kept Mountain, Clifftop Retreat and Dragonskull Summit and cast Zuko on turn 3 exactly as planned.

Game 0052: the kept hand was Fire Nation Palace, Mountain and Plains with four red spells and no black source. Electro and Headliner Scarlett carried rounds 3 and 4, but Zuko could not be cast until Command Tower was drawn and played in round 6, and he came down in round 7.

claim: On a turn you expect one opponent to take 7 or more damage, leave Spinerock Knoll untapped and tap your other lands first. Its {R} can be paid with firebending mana during combat damage, so only the Knoll itself has to stay untapped. That lets you play the hidden card free that same turn.
evidence: Game 0041, round 5: the Soldier hit Tidus for 8, but the Knoll had been tapped to pay for the Axe equip, so the Daydreamer under it stayed put (the pilot's note: 'one mana short'). Round 6: the Knoll was left untapped, the Soldier hit Mothman for 8, and one of the floating firebending red activated the Knoll to put Goliath Daydreamer into play for free.

claim: While Zuko can't be cast or is off the table, a firebending token can still carry the game. Put Two-Handed Axe and Fire Nation Turret's +2/+0 and firebending 2 on the token from Firebender Ascension. Once Ascension has 4 quest counters it copies each firebending trigger, so every attack makes double red. Spend red with no other use on Untimely Malfunction to stop blockers, then sink the rest into Turret charge counters before combat ends. (Game 0041, rounds 5 and 6: the Soldier was 8 power with Turret and Axe. In round 7 the Turret went on Hellkite Charger and the Soldier hit for 4.)
evidence: Game 0041, rounds 5 to 7: the 2/2 Soldier became 8 power each turn (Turret 4, Axe doubled). In round 6, Ascension's copies turned 3 red into 6. Two of that paid Untimely Malfunction so Ruin Crab and Vexing Radgull couldn't block, and the Soldier connected for 8. This seat did 29 damage without ever casting its commander. (Put right by the fact check: The Soldier was 8 power only in rounds 5 and 6. In round 7 (table turn 25), the Turret's +2/+0 and firebending 2 went on Hellkite Charger. The Soldier was 4 power (2 doubled by the Axe) and dealt 4.)

claim: When Fire Lord Zuko dies or is exiled, move him to the command zone (you may do this whenever he goes to your graveyard or exile) and recast him for {R}{W}{B} plus {2} tax. He is never lost to the graveyard. After he dies, check each turn whether you have 5 or more mana for him before spending it on anything else.
evidence: Game 0051: Fleshbag Marauder made the pilot sacrifice Zuko on table turn 15 (round 4). The pilot left him in the graveyard and wrote 'Zuko is in my graveyard, not the command zone, so I can't recast him' in rounds 5 and 6 and in its end notes. From round 5 on it had 6 to 9 mana sources, and in round 10 it ended with 9 untapped and an empty hand. It never cast its commander again.

claim: Cast Zuko before you play or cast anything that impulse draw, Bonehoard Dracosaur or Light Up the Stage has exiled. Play the exiled land after he resolves, and hold exiled flash cards like Embercleave until combat, so every one of them puts a +1/+1 counter on your team.
evidence: Game 0052, round 7 (table turn 25): Dracosaur's upkeep trigger exiled a Swamp and Embercleave. The pilot cast Zuko first, then played the Swamp from exile (+1/+1 counters on its creatures), then attacked and flashed in Embercleave from exile for 4 with two attackers (a second counter each). In round 8 it played Dragonskull Summit from Commune with Lava's exile after Zuko was out, which gave a third counter.

claim: Heartfire Hero has valiant, so the first spell or ability of yours aimed at it each turn puts a +1/+1 counter on it. Aim Fire Nation Palace's firebending 4 at it before combat, and use it as the source for Chandra's Ignition (on a turn it hasn't yet been targeted). The counter goes on before Ignition resolves, so the Hero deals one more damage to each opponent.
evidence: Game 0052, round 8: Palace targeting Hero gave it a counter plus firebending 4, and those 4 red helped pay for Commune with Lava. Round 9 (table turn 32): the pilot recast the Hero for {R}, then aimed Chandra's Ignition at it. The valiant counter made it 2/2, and 2 damage took Tidus from 2 to 0 to win the game. (Put right by the fact check: Heartfire Hero's valiant only triggers the first time each turn it becomes the target of a spell or ability you control. Later targets that turn add no counter. In the record it got exactly one valiant counter per turn: from Fire Nation Palace on turn 29 and from Chandra's Ignition on turn 32. Both were the first time it was targeted that turn.)
